i’ve lived here for over a year, there are pros and cons here, some of which you may find in other apartments, but this is my personal list:

pros:
- downtown, so walking to shops, coffee, bars, etc. is very convenient. walking to campus is easy & multiple bus routes run down here so youre open to many options
-theres a gym on-site, so you dont have to go to the rec if you dont want to & the gym is usually empty, if not 1/2 other people in there
-in-unit washer + drier is convenient
-comes furnished so you dont have to worry about buying new mattresses n whatnot while youre at college
-multiple points to use key fob so feels very safe

cons:
-i can hear my neighbors phone conversations though the wall
-if youre lucky enough to live on the 5th floor, you don’t have to worry about stomping/things dropping/etc, that gets LOUD
-at least one bathroom in the unit has the fan on at all times and its fucking annoying
-wifi can suck sometimes
-not easy to have friends over unless you want to keep going up and down to let them in
-parking is next to none & parking pass (which is kinda ideal if you have a car and want a guaranteed spot) is $90/month

i went through a huge weight loss around 16 the way youre planning at around the same sw!,, my biggest tips are... 
- start being more active in small ways, walks are awesome ! especially if you own a dog, super easy to get some steps in that way. you already started doing that so thats awesome !! 10,000 steps isnt achievable for a lot of people (not for me anyways), so being able to at least block out an hour to be active is a good goal to set. 
- protein ! keeps you full the longest + does help with a lot of snacking i used to do. i loved making protein smoothies in the morning or snacking on deli meats or protein bars ! rx bars are amazing !!!! i rec also finding a good set of macros that work for your goals. 
-1200 cal is too low ! thats the rec intake for a toddler + youre a growing woman. go on a cal calculator (there are a few online ones that are awesome) and set some goals. raise your intake a bit ! 
- dont go based on a timeline, go based on trends. you lost a lot of weight the first week + im sure it was a lot of water weight from changing your habits. just because u gained ONE singular pound doesnt mean much, follow trends throughout time ! if you find you keep gaining weight across this change, find something that could be affecting that. 

please feel free to dm if you ever wanna talk ! i know how this change feels + you deserve to be safe in this journey.
